Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] Untested theorycraft with low confidence, and the reason for the low confidence is simple: 3.2.0's Paladin section describes its Holy-line changes without publishing a single number. Holy Bolt is adjusted, Blessed Shield is adjusted, Judgement is redesigned - that is the whole of it, in every source consulted. The argument for building around them anyway is that they are, together with the +30% core-stat scalar, literally everything 3.2.0 gives the class, and the class's carried-forward build collects none of them. A patch that redesigns a skill is usually telling you where it wants the class to go. This page takes that hint and builds the Holy character, on the understanding that it is a hint rather than a number. If the redesigned Judgement is weak, this build is weak, and no amount of gearing fixes it.

Rotation
  1. Auras up, Clash on cooldown for Resolve, Blessed Shield held down as the main cast, Holy Bolt on cooldown.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Auras up, Clash for Resolve, Blessed Shield as the main cast, Holy Bolt on cooldown - and go and read what the redesigned Judgement actually does, because that sentence does not exist anywhere yet and this whole page is waiting on it.
Move on when [ptr] Level 70 (Mrak, on the PTR) and the redesigned Judgement read and written down.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Blessed Shield held down, Holy Bolt on cooldown, Clash for Resolve, auras up. Measure Blessed Shield against the Thorns build here rather than at the end, and slot Judgement in place of Holy Bolt in game to compare the two.
Move on when [ptr] A measured comparison against paladin-hybrid-shield-charge-holy on the same character.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Unchanged. Record the comparison.
Move on when [ptr] The comparison is done and the Holy line is worth building around. If Judgement's redesign turned out to be small, say so and play the hybrid instead.

Pushing — [ptr] Untested at push tiers and untested on this patch. The honest position is that this page is a bet on a redesign nobody has published, and the first person to read Judgement in game knows more about this build than this page does.

Uniques
  • offhand [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts, which is the right way to gear an experiment. Live route: Astaroth, at the end of Escalating Nightmare Dungeons, Torment 1+; 1x Escalation Sigil. Where →
  • ring 1 [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Echo of Varshan, Malignant Burrow near the Tree of Whispers waypoint, Hawezar, Torment 1+; 1x Lair Key. Its Judgement damage went 80-100% to 100-150% in 3.1.x - whether that survived 3.2.0's Judgement redesign is test 3 and is unknown. Where →
  • chest [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Harbinger of Hatred, Nahantu near the Kurast Docks waypoint; 1x Greater Lair Key. It pays per Resolve consumed, which is why the Resolve engine is kept even though the damage skill has changed. Where →

Point allocation, in order65 points across 6 nodes

[ptr] Provenance, stated plainly. No 3.2.0 skill tree is published for any build of this class anywhere: the official notes carry no allocations, and Maxroll, Icy Veins, d4builds and d4guides were all still serving Season 14 guides when the PTR digest was written. InfinityBuilds now carries Season 15 PTR builds, but only Warlock ones. This allocation is therefore the specialist's, built from the skill list knowledge/ptr/season-15.md authorises for this class plus the 3.2.0 changes that actually apply. Treat the point counts as a starting shape to test, not as a published build.

Skill point priority

  1. [ptr] Blessed Shield first - it is one of the three Holy skills 3.2.0 touches and it is the only one that can carry a bar
  2. Both auras next: Fanaticism Aura is where Vulnerable, Weaken and Fortify come from and gives 14% critical strike chance at 15 ranks
  3. Holy Bolt on the bar from the start - it is the second of the three Holy skills 3.2.0 adjusts and, unlike Judgement, it exists as a node in this repo's pinned 3.1.0 game database, so the site can actually draw it. Judgement is discussed everywhere on this page and appears on no bar for exactly that reason: the feed carries no Paladin skill by that name, and putting one there would name a node that resolves to nothing
  4. Clash for Resolve, Fortress for Unstoppable

Build Notes (Shared for all Variants)

PTR - subject to change before Season 15 launches; every claim here is 3.2.0 test-build data and must be re-verified at launch. [ptr] Untested theorycraft with low confidence, and the reason for the low confidence is simple: 3.2.0's Paladin section describes its Holy-line changes without publishing a single number. Holy Bolt is adjusted, Blessed Shield is adjusted, Judgement is redesigned - that is the whole of it, in every source consulted. The argument for building around them anyway is that they are, together with the +30% core-stat scalar, literally everything 3.2.0 gives the class, and the class's carried-forward build collects none of them. A patch that redesigns a skill is usually telling you where it wants the class to go. This page takes that hint and builds the Holy character, on the understanding that it is a hint rather than a number. If the redesigned Judgement is weak, this build is weak, and no amount of gearing fixes it.

Rotation
  1. Auras up, Clash on cooldown for Resolve, Blessed Shield held down as the main cast, Holy Bolt on cooldown.
Variants

Leveling — [ptr] Auras up, Clash for Resolve, Blessed Shield as the main cast, Holy Bolt on cooldown - and go and read what the redesigned Judgement actually does, because that sentence does not exist anywhere yet and this whole page is waiting on it.
Move on when [ptr] Level 70 (Mrak, on the PTR) and the redesigned Judgement read and written down.

Early Endgame — [ptr] Blessed Shield held down, Holy Bolt on cooldown, Clash for Resolve, auras up. Measure Blessed Shield against the Thorns build here rather than at the end, and slot Judgement in place of Holy Bolt in game to compare the two.
Move on when [ptr] A measured comparison against paladin-hybrid-shield-charge-holy on the same character.

Late Endgame — [ptr] Unchanged. Record the comparison.
Move on when [ptr] The comparison is done and the Holy line is worth building around. If Judgement's redesign turned out to be small, say so and play the hybrid instead.

Pushing — [ptr] Untested at push tiers and untested on this patch. The honest position is that this page is a bet on a redesign nobody has published, and the first person to read Judgement in game knows more about this build than this page does.

Uniques
  • offhand [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts, which is the right way to gear an experiment. Live route: Astaroth, at the end of Escalating Nightmare Dungeons, Torment 1+; 1x Escalation Sigil. Where →
  • ring 1 [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Echo of Varshan, Malignant Burrow near the Tree of Whispers waypoint, Hawezar, Torment 1+; 1x Lair Key. Its Judgement damage went 80-100% to 100-150% in 3.1.x - whether that survived 3.2.0's Judgement redesign is test 3 and is unknown. Where →
  • chest [ptr] PTR route: Mrak's boosts. Live route: Harbinger of Hatred, Nahantu near the Kurast Docks waypoint; 1x Greater Lair Key. It pays per Resolve consumed, which is why the Resolve engine is kept even though the damage skill has changed. Where →

Reasoning

Hypothesis[ptr] 3.2.0's Holy-line work is where Paladin's 3.2.0 build is meant to be. The patch gives the class exactly two things - a +30% core-stat scalar and adjustments to Holy Bolt, Blessed Shield and a redesigned Judgement - and the class's existing build, Shield Charge Thorns, collects only the first. A build whose damage runs through the Holy skills collects both. The Resolve engine, the auras and the block package all carry over unchanged, because 3.2.0 does not touch Resolve, Retribution, Clash, Fortress or either aura, so the change is confined to the delivery skills.
Confidencelow
How to test it[ptr] (1) Read the redesigned Judgement in game and write down what it actually does. No source publishes it and the entire build hangs off it; everything below is provisional until that sentence exists. (2) Measure Blessed Shield's damage against Shield Charge's Thorns on the same character - Paladin's damage on this class's published build is Physical Thorns delivered by Retribution pulses, not weapon hits, so a Holy build is a different damage type as well as a different skill and the two may not be comparable at all. (3) Check whether Seal of the Second Trumpet's Judgement damage - already raised from 80-100% to 100-150% back in 3.1.x - survived the redesign, since a redesigned skill can silently invalidate a unique built for the old one. (4) Confirm the Resolve engine still works when Shield Charge is off the bar: Resolve comes from Defiance Aura plus Clash, and Clash stays, so it should. (5) Compare against paladin-hybrid-shield-charge-holy, which is the conservative version of the same idea and keeps the Thorns engine.

Provoke

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 25 seconds

Raheir Taunts enemies around you for 5 seconds. You gain 5% Damage Reduction for each target, up to 20%.

Ground Slam

Core skillRaheir

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Round Shield

Basic Attack: Shield Strike

Raheir brutalizes the ground, dealing 160% Physical damage and Slowing enemies by 30% for 6 seconds. Targets in the center of the slam are Slowed by 60% instead.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Raheir swings a round shield at enemies, dealing 85% Physical damage. Every 20 swings, Raheir Heals you for 8% of your Maximum Life.

Shield Charge

Core skillRaheir

Cooldown: 11 seconds

Weapon: Tower Shield

Basic Attack: Shield Bash

Raheir rushes forward aggressively, dealing 110% Physical damage and Taunting nearby enemies for 4 seconds.

Selecting a Mercenary Core Skill alters their wielded Weapon and Basic Attack.

Raheir bashes enemies with a tower shield, dealing 80% Physical damage and Fortifying you for 0.2% of your Maximum Life.

Crater

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Raheir strikes the ground 3 times, each burst dealing 30% Physical damage and Pulling In enemies. The final burst deals 40% more Physical damage and additionally Stuns enemies for 2 seconds.

Raheir's Guard

PassiveRaheir

Raheir grants you 15%[+] Armor.

Vanguard

PassiveRaheir

Raheir Slows surrounding enemies by 40%.

Mocking Lure

PassiveRaheir

You deal 15%[x] increased damage to enemies Taunted by Raheir.

Iron Wolf's Ward

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he Knocks Back Close enemies and Taunts Distant enemies for 4 seconds.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Iron Wolf's Call

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, your next 4 Core Skills within 10 seconds deal 25%[x] increased damage and cost no Resource.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 25%.

Sundering Shield

PassiveRaheir

Raheir's final Crater burst deals 200%[x] increased damage and inflicts Vulnerable on enemies for 4 seconds.

Shield Throw

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 22 seconds

Raheir throws his shield, dealing 450% Physical damage and Taunting enemies for 5 seconds. The shield bounces up to 9 times and cannot bounce to the same target twice.

Iron Wolf's Arrival

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he also casts Ground Slam and Shield Throw.

Raheir's Valiance's Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Consecrated Shield

PassiveRaheir

Raheir's Shield Throw Consecrates enemies for 6 seconds. Directly damaging a Consecrated enemy Heals you for 6% of your Maximum Life, once per target.

Bastion

Iconic skillRaheir

Cooldown: 30 seconds

Raheir takes a protective position for 5 seconds, redirecting 90% of the damage that would be dealt to surrounding allies to himself for 5 seconds.

Bastion's initial cast also grants surrounding allies Unstoppable for 1.0 seconds.

Iron Wolf's Virtue

PassiveRaheir

When Raheir's Valiance is triggered, he Heals you for 25% of your Maximum Life.

Raheir's Valiance Cooldown is reduced by 35%.

Inspiration

PassiveRaheir

Enemies affected by Raheir's Ground Slam take 15%[x] increased damage.

Allies affected by Raheir's Bastion deal 25%[x] increased damage.

Raheir's Aegis

PassiveRaheir

Raheir grants you 15% Resistance to All Elements.

Draw Fire

PassiveRaheir

When you use a Healing Potion, Raheir Taunts enemies around him for 4 seconds. Can only occur once every 20 seconds.
